text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Lithuanian parliament voted on Tuesday to liquidate Innovation bank.
- Lithuania's foreign debt in hard currency was $1.212 billion on April 1, 1997.
- Siemens affiliate Baltijos Automobiliu Technika will become the first to set up in the Klaipeda free economy zone, the executive director of the zone, Judita Simonavichiute, said.
- Austrian Creditanstalt Investment Bank is examining the financial markets of the three Baltic countries. The results of the research are expected at the beginning of June.
- The year on year inflation in March was 8.3 percent, the statistics department said.
- The Lithuanian parliament wants to appeal to NATO countries to start negotiations with at least one Baltic country during the first phase of the alliance's expansion.
- Toyota Motor Co dealers in Lithuania have sold 451 new cars over the past four years.
- Lithuanian Social Democrats strongly object to the government's rapid moves to privatise large enterprises in the energy, communication and transport sectors.
- The Lithuanian government intends to impose big fines on companies who employ people without necessary contracts.
- Preliminary statistics data show that Lithuania's GDP grew by 3.6 percent last year.

- The newspaper publishes a list of the 50 biggest exporters in Lithuania. The top exporters are Achema (furtilisers), Ekranas (TV screens), Lifosa (fertilisers), Dirbtinis Pluoshtas (acetite yarn), Snaige (fridges), Marijampole tinned milk, Alytaus Textile, Drobe and Kuro aparatura.
